column1: # Divinity: Original Sin 2 - Definitive Edition: Larian Studios' Divinity Engine (FW3.5), SDK 8.2.0, NVN, Wwise sound, RakNet 15.03.26; update 1.0.3.1 (v196608).
# Its shaders are in the .bshd files of Data/*.pak, Larian's LSPK packages (shader_split.py lspk_shaders).
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and brought up on Android (README.md)
# the NPDM declares 4 MB of system resource (virtual address memory) and main sets a heap: a 5 GB block with a large alias region; the heap check sizes the heap region from the heap the game asks for
# the NPDM declares 4 MB of system resource
# Single player is a RakNet server and a client in one process, talking UDP over 127.0.0.1: on New Game the server opens its socket (main+0x1adc06c), and with no socket it
# sat in its LoadSession state while the client waited in StartServer, at the loading screen. A Switch with no network still has loopback, so the game gets it (hle_loopback.c)
# Shadow maps, for DM_VK_SKIP_SHADOWS=1 on Android (a player's choice, off by default: gfx_vk_shadow.inc). The game's sun casts into a 1536x1536 D16 map on the title screen,
# the menus and in character creation (pass profiles on a OnePlus Pad 3, 2026-11-10), with no other square depth-only pass there; a tester's patch that left out square depth
# passes of 512 or more ran Fort Joy faster and cooler on an Adreno 735 (issue #113). Fort Joy's maps are not measured: the log's "shadow map … set as the target" lines name them
# the game asked for a 2.96 GB heap: a 3.000 GB heap region
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 in the check boot: the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# heap check: 2026-11-09, the heap request did not fit, then heap 2.96 GB; set mem_alias, depth_mode

# address regions: 2026-11-09, in its first 15 s in nnMain the game's regions reach alias +1.40 GB, within the profile's 1.50 GB alias region (what it takes later in play is not measured here) (rewrite a3c790c419d0)
